business_problem: Autodesk needed a more scalable and flexible data platform for Product Insights so it could capture growing volumes of product-usage data, analyze changing user behavior, and deliver personalized guidance to customers without the capacity limits of its prior object-store and metastore design.
solution_summary: Autodesk built Product Insights on MongoDB Atlas to collect usage events from its software portfolio and turn them into personalized recommendations for end users. Atlas integrates with Autodesk's broader infrastructure and stores analytics data in flexible documents, which lets teams retrieve product activity and generate insights across emails, web portals, and in-product pop-ups from the same operational store. That document model also absorbs new schemas as user behavior and service requirements change, removing the rigidity that constrained the earlier object-store and metastore approach. Because Atlas provides managed scalability, resiliency, and operational tooling out of the box, Autodesk's engineers spend less time on infrastructure work and more time refining the recommendation experience. MongoDB's integration with GraphQL also helped Autodesk improve API accuracy while maintaining subsecond latency for a service that now delivers several million insights every week.

solution_components.name: MongoDB Atlas
solution_components.role: Stores Autodesk's product-usage analytics in a flexible document model and powers the Product Insights recommendation platform.

data_flow: Usage data from Autodesk products is captured into MongoDB Atlas, organized as product-level documents, analyzed to identify helpful recommendations, and then surfaced to users through emails, web portals, and in-software pop-ups with subsecond API responses.
business_outcome: Autodesk scaled Product Insights by 300% in one year, now delivers several million insights weekly, achieves subsecond API latency, and can extend personalized guidance to more users without increasing operational overhead.
